confidence_note: Revised after verification: OXO/Good Grips could not be tied to Pink's text (no source found). Story now rests on Pink's design chapter as reported by summaries: functionality alone no longer enough (Oprah excerpt), iPod vs MP3 players with more functionality, design notebook, four graphic-design principles (contrast, repetition, alignment, proximity). The kettle example is the writer's own, flagged as such.
facts: Design is the first of Pink's six senses.
Merely functional is no longer enough; beautiful, whimsical or emotionally engaging matters economically and personally.
With material wants met, function stops differentiating; chapter summaries cite the iPod's dominance over MP3 players with more functionality.
Pink suggests a design notebook for good and bad everyday design, and sketching a better version when an appliance frustrates you.
Pink recommends following design magazines and museums.
Four basic graphic design principles: contrast, repetition, alignment, proximity.
scene_details: A peeler with a wide, soft, non-slip handle
A hand with stiff joints holding a thin handle
A thick, soft handle with ridges
tension: A product designed for a small group with hard-to-use tools ended up preferred by everyone.
opening_idea: Start with the peeler's handle in the hand.

lessons.idea: Design starts with the person who struggles most; solving their problem often makes the thing better for everyone.
lessons.anchor: The Oxo peeler's wide soft handle was meant for arthritic hands and was bought by many more people.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A clinic that rewrites its appointment form so an older patient can fill it in, and finds every patient finishes it faster.

reflect_final: Who struggles most with the thing you make or run, and what small change would make it easier for that person?

use_cases.situation: Your team is reviewing a product page.
use_cases.move: The Oxo handle was designed for hands that struggle. Ask: who would find this hardest, and what would help them?

use_cases.situation: You are choosing a gift for an older relative.
use_cases.move: Pick the version with easy grips or big buttons.

use_cases.situation: You are about to send a document.
use_cases.move: Reread it as a first-time reader would and fix the first thing that is hard to follow.

pocket_idea: A peeler made for arthritic hands became everyone's favourite; design for the person with the hardest time.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A peeler made for arthritic hands was bought by people without arthritis too, because it felt better.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: In A Whole New Mind, Pink says design now matters because plenty of products already work. A peeler with a wide, soft, non-slip handle was made for arthritic hands and bought by many others. Design starts with who uses it and what is hard for them.
